---
title: "Blue MCP"
---

Blue's Model Context Protocol (MCP) server lets a compatible local client inspect the active project and engine. With read-write access, the client can also request supported project edits, timeline playback, and WAV renders.

## Install and enable

1. Install a Blue 3 build that includes **Settings… → MCP**. MCP ships with the desktop app. Check [Blue releases](https://github.com/kunstmusik/blue/releases) for your platform or use the [development build artifacts](https://github.com/kunstmusik/blue/actions/workflows/develop.yml) after the feature lands. Install [Csound 7](https://csound.com/download.html) if you want playback or rendering.
2. Launch Blue and open a project. On macOS, open **Settings…** from the **Blue** menu. On Windows and Linux, open it from **File**.
3. Select **MCP**, check **Enable MCP Server**, keep **Access Mode** set to **Read-only**, and click **Apply**. Wait for **Listening** and use the endpoint displayed there. If the preferred port is occupied, Blue shows the fallback port.
4. Choose your client under **Credentials and Client Configuration**, then click **Copy Client Config**. Keep Blue running while using the connection.

## Connect a client

The server uses Streamable HTTP on IPv4 loopback. Use a client that runs on the same machine as Blue and can send the bearer token. For a custom client, use the displayed URL and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with the credential from **Copy Credential**.

| Client | Add the copied configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Cursor | Merge the `blue` entry into `mcpServers` in your local `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. The snippet contains the actual token. Keep that file private and outside shared source control. |
| VS Code | Use a local VS Code session that supports editor-managed MCP and interactive inputs. Run **MCP: Open User Configuration** and merge the snippet into that file, or use a private workspace’s `.vscode/mcp.json`. Start the server connection and paste the raw value from **Copy Credential** when VS Code prompts. |
| Codex CLI | Add the copied `[mcp_servers.blue]` table to your local Codex `config.toml`. Set `BLUE_MCP_TOKEN` in the environment of the process that starts Codex, then start or restart Codex. The TOML references the variable by name. |

For client-specific options, see the [Cursor MCP documentation](https://cursor.com/docs/mcp) and the [VS Code MCP configuration reference](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/reference/mcp-configuration).

Refresh client discovery after switching access modes or restarting the listener. If the port changes, copy the configuration again. An authentication error usually means the client needs the current token. **Rotate Credential** invalidates the previous token and closes its sessions. If Blue displays **Session-only**, copy a new token when you next launch Blue. Disable MCP and click **Apply** when you want to close the listener.

## Inspect the active project

Start with a prompt such as “Use Blue’s `get_project_summary` tool and summarize the active project without editing it.” The client can also read the instrument list, inspect score objects, and read the engine status and recent console messages.

Ask the client to run `generate_csd` to inspect a disk-profile Csound document. Blue refuses observation-only generation for projects that need script execution, external lookups, or work beyond its inspection limits. Open an active project if the client reports that none is available.

## Edit, play, and render

Switch **Access Mode** to **Read-write** and click **Apply** when you want the client to make changes. The client must use the current document receipt for writes. If Blue reports a conflict, ask the client to reread the project and confirm the intended edit before retrying. Supported edits appear in Blue's undo history. Save the project in Blue to persist them.

Playback and renders can prompt for approval in the desktop app. For a render, ask for a fresh WAV basename such as `preview.wav`. The client can use the saved project's working directory or ask Blue to display a local folder picker. Blue publishes the result only in the approved directory and refuses an existing file. You can choose another volume if it supports private staging and atomic publication. On macOS, a render to another volume can leave one empty, private scratch file in the approved directory. If Blue rejects a volume, try a different local folder. Keep Csound 7 available and check **Settings… → Realtime Render → Check Engine and Csound** if the engine reports an error.
